newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares lose ground after government crumbles.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares lose ground after government crumbles.

text.p: Delhi shares lost ground in a special trading session on Saturday following the government's fall, but brokers said the decline was moderated by expectations the 1997/98 budget might clear parliament.
The Delhi Stock Exchange sensitive index ended 8.69 points down at 753.05 points.

"Selling by operators who made speculative purchases yesterday in anticipation of the survival of the government aided nervous selling in view of its collapse," said Sanjay Mittal of stockbrokers SRM Securities.
"With this kind of uncertainty over the formation of the government, foreign buyers might not come in to buy for the time being," another broker said.
Shares of Reliance Industries ended 4.10 rupees down at 265 rupees. State Bank of India fell six rupees to 272 rupees. Cement-maker ACC dropped 34 rupees to 1,356 rupees.
TELCO shares plunged 20.10 rupees to 372.90 rupees while Bajaj Auto Ltd fell 16 rupees to 942 rupees.
Larsen and Toubro fell four rupees to 211, BSES Ltd dropped 3.85 to 221.15, MTNL eight rupees to 270, and Ranbaxy Labs nine rupees to 650 rupees.
Shares of ITC Ltd fell 6.10 rupees to 392.55, Nestle shares fell two rupees to 228. Hindustan Lever rose 11 rupees to 1,036 rupees.
